note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §6 Pistons, §13.7, Stage 79; asked for by the user, 2026-11-27) on data/benches/syringes.json: a syringe's plunger is pushed by the hand, held back by what is inside. A sealed syringe of water does not give; one of air gives and springs back; two of water joined move together; two of air joined move together, the air between giving a little.
title: Experiment: syringes

steps.title: Push the water
steps.text: Drag the handle of the left syringe, the one of water, down as far as you can, then let go.
steps.why: Dragging a handle pushes its plunger with your hand's force: as hard as it takes, up to what a hand can push, about 80 N.

checks.text: pushed as hard as a hand can

steps.title: It hardly moved
steps.text: Read where its plunger stands now: on the scale, as it was.
steps.why: A liquid's molecules already touch: pushing them closer takes far more force than a hand has. The plunger moved by the bubble of air in it, a tenth of a millilitre, and no more.

steps.title: Push the air
steps.text: Drag the handle of the second syringe, of air, down as far as it goes, and let go.
steps.why: A gas's molecules are far apart: it gives. As it is squeezed, more of them hit the plunger each second and the pressure rises, until it pushes back as hard as your hand does.

steps.title: It springs back
steps.text: Watch the plunger once you let go.
steps.why: Let go, the squeezed air pushes the plunger back out until it is at the room's pressure again: nearly where it started, a little short, held by the plunger's friction (and the air warmed a little by the push cools back).

steps.title: Push one
steps.text: The two syringes of water in the middle are joined nozzle to nozzle by a tube. Drag the left one's handle down to 20 mL and let go.
steps.why: The water cannot be squeezed, so what leaves one syringe must go into the other: its plunger is pushed out as far as yours goes in. This is how hydraulics work: brakes, lifts, diggers.

checks.text: the other pushed out past 55 mL

steps.title: Push one
steps.text: Now the two syringes of air on the right, joined the same way. Drag the left one's handle down to 20 mL and let go.
steps.why: The air carries the push too, but it gives first: the pressure must rise before it moves the other plunger, so the other follows a moment behind yours, and does not end exactly where yours left off.

checks.text: the other pushed out past 70 mL

steps.title: Not quite in step
steps.text: Compare the two: add the readings of the joined syringes of air.
steps.why: Together they hold the same air at nearly the room's pressure, so their volumes add up to about 100 mL; not exactly, as friction lets each stop a little early and the push warmed the air.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged
